idiom_name: SQLAlchemy Session (unit of work, flush at commit) with deferred autoflush
implementation_notes: SQLAlchemy's Session is the persistence context: mapped objects are instrumented, attribute changes are recorded against the identity map, and pending INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are executed by a flush that normally runs before a query and, at the latest, at commit. The deferral is explicit - Session(autoflush=False) keeps intermediate states in memory until session.flush()/session.commit(), and repeated modifications of one object coalesce into a single UPDATE. What replaces the classic structure: the ORM's unit of work; Django's ORM has no deferred change set (each save is one statement), so there the buffer is hand-written. The classic manual form is justified only for stores without an ORM.
code_sketch:
with Session(engine, autoflush=False) as session, session.begin():
    user = session.get(User, 1)
    user.email = "new@example.com"    # staged, no SQL yet
    user.last_seen = datetime.now()   # coalesced with the line above
    # session.flush()  # force now if a later query must see the change
# commit flushes once: a single UPDATE for this user
pitfalls: A Session is not thread-safe and must be request-scoped; a long-lived session accumulates identity-map entries and unbounded pending state.
With autoflush=False a query can silently return pre-change rows - call session.flush() before reads that must observe the write.
After commit the session expires objects by default; reading them outside the transaction triggers re-SELECTs (or DetachedInstanceError if the session is closed).
